sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Munich prices street parking by a city ordinance and keeps resident permits at a state-set cap. The Parkgebührenordnung, last amended on 15 August 2023, sets Rate 1 at €2.50 an hour for the Altstadt from 08:00 to 23:00 and for the Hauptbahnhof zone, and Rate 2 at €2.00 an hour elsewhere and in the Altstadt outside those hours, with a daily maximum of €11 where no time limit is posted [1]. The annual resident permit is capped by Bavaria at €30.70. In February 2025 the Interior Ministry told the news agency dpa that there would continue to be no new regulation raising it; the ministry had put the reform on hold in 2023, citing high inflation, and Munich was among the cities in a dpa survey that favoured a higher cap [3].

The central decision is the council's 'Altstadt für alle' principle resolution of 17 December 2025, which passed against the votes of the CSU and several other groups [4]. It orders detailed planning for a traffic concept for the Graggenauer Viertel and the eastern Angerviertel and asks that the concept also examine a multilingual digital parking guidance system, short-term parking of 10 minutes instead of 3, a check of the public authority garages for use by residents and visitors, and how live occupancy data of all garages could be provided as an interim step [4][5]. Those are tasks and questions, not yet measures. The 2026–2032 coalition agreement of Mayor Dominik Krause, which we date to May 2026 from its file details, states aims: allow private parking towers, open company garages and supermarket car parks to neighbours at night, add park-and-ride capacity with neighbouring municipalities, allow pavement parking where locally necessary and support parking guidance systems [6]. A June 2021 draft Mobilitätsstrategie 2035 had named three steering pillars for parking: supply, management of existing supply, and demand [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Park-and-ride is where the sourced activity is. The city-owned P+R Park & Ride GmbH looks after 38 P+R sites with more than 14,000 spaces in Munich and the surrounding area; its daily fees are roughly €1 to €2, and stays over 24 hours are provided only at six sites [13]. In March 2022 it looked after more than 9,500 spaces in the city itself, of which 7,233 were P+R, 1,469 in nine resident garages and 1,141 in other city car parks [12]. The wider MVV area has P+R at 187 stations with about 32,000 spaces (2024), and the P+R guide says information, fees and rules are not standardised and some places need more capacity [14]. In May 2025 the CSU and Freie Wähler council group tabled a motion asking the P+R company to show occupancy and nearby alternative parking at its sites; it is a motion, not a decision [24].

On the private side, Q-Park completed the purchase of Bavaria Parkgaragen on 30 June 2025: 26 car parks with more than 12,000 spaces and 174 charging points, mainly in Munich, Berlin, Düsseldorf and other German cities; the release does not list which Munich garages are included [15]. SWM announced on 22 April 2026 that 154 charging points at the Olympiapark Parkharfe were commissioned, 86 AC and 68 DC [22]. We found no sourced figures on a move of parking to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Munich price and capacity listings cover 48 car parks with 40,788 spaces, which are the garages we hold, not all of the city's parking. They come from operator listings: 18 APCOA with 25,113 spaces, 26 Q-Park with 14,162 and four Contipark with 1,513. APCOA's total is dominated by event and out-of-centre sites such as the Allianz Arena (10,700 spaces) and Messe München (4,650), and its median garage lies 6.3 km from the centre, against 2.5 km for Q-Park and 0.8 km for Contipark. The median hourly rate across the city is €3.30. Contipark is dearest at a median of €4.90 an hour and €38.50 a day, against €3.50 and €35 for Q-Park and €3.00 and €25 for APCOA. The four garages within 500 m of a station have 2,025 spaces and a median rate of €3.65.

The Hauptbahnhof shows how far prices differ. Its own page lists eleven parking options; only the Hauptbahnhof Süd garage (242 spaces, €3.30 an hour, €32 a day) is listed under DB BahnPark, while Marsstraße (701 spaces, €4 and €40) and Hopfenpost (583 spaces, €3 and €17) appear without operators named [19]. The Allianz Arena car park is open only during events, at €12 to €20 on match days and €5 with the first 45 minutes free on other days [20]. The Stachus garage has 700 spaces and links to a Contipark page [16].

Occupancy is measured only at park-and-ride, and only partly. We found no open occupancy feed for the central garages, and the council's December 2025 decision asks how live occupancy of all garages could be provided as an interim step [5]. Since 7 October 2026 we collect, every 30 minutes, the counts that the MVV's park-and-ride map publishes for 15 Munich facilities with 5,659 spaces. Only three of the 15 show counts that change: Studentenstadt (405 spaces), Innsbrucker Ring (95) and the open-air lot at Fürstenried West (50). A fourth, Aidenbachstraße, delivered changing counts until 8 October and has since stopped reporting in real time. The other 11, including Allach, Moosach, Fröttmaning, Neuperlach Süd, Olympiazentrum and Heimeranplatz, have shown one and the same number at every reading from 7 October to 21 October, with a fresh timestamp each time, so we treat them as stuck sensor outputs, not as occupancy; the evening snapshot of 7 October that we first published for them is withdrawn. For the three working sites, about two weeks of data show Studentenstadt at 30% on weekdays and 22% at weekends, with a highest reading of 60%; Innsbrucker Ring at 28% and 20%, highest reading 55%; and the Fürstenried West lot at 47% and 34%, with a highest reading of 96% on a Thursday at about 10:00. The window covers term time at the Studentenstadt but is short.

The city's December 2024 forecast rates Allach, Moosach, Neuperlach Süd and Fröttmaning green, meaning more than 75% of spaces free, in every time band [25]. The forecast expects weekday pressure at Fürstenried West (red, under 10% free, from 08:00 to 16:00), Olympiazentrum and Großhadern (09:00 to 14:00), and Aidenbachstraße and Trudering-Süd (10:00 to 14:00) [25]. Of the facilities the forecast mentions, only the Fürstenried West lot gives usable counts in our feed; its 96% peak on a weekday morning fits the red rating for 08:00 to 16:00, which concerns the whole Fürstenried West site, and the other sites cannot be compared because their counts are stuck, stopped or absent.
